memory_candidates.content: When a shell test suite's default subject resolution is deploy-tree-first (a copy of the deployed .claude/scripts/ tree), exercising a pre-redeploy source-store edit requires a dedicated source-store-first resolved variable, sourced fresh inside its own subshell -- never the suite-level sourced functions, which would silently exercise the stale deployed copy. Mirror an existing Group 5/6-style pattern in the same suite rather than inventing a new one; and if the edit under test calls a SECOND script via a bare relative path (e.g. skill-base.sh invoking .claude/scripts/update-task-status.sh), that second script's fixture copy must ALSO be overridden from the source store, or its own stale gate will reject the call before the first edit is ever exercised.

update-task-status.sh's postflight/implement path has a plan-file-completion-stamp step (writes [COMPLETED] to the plan's Status line) that runs independently of --phase-check -- it fires even when --phase-check is absent, and refuses with an unrelated error if no plan directory/file is resolvable for the task. Any fixture exercising postflight/implement (directly or via skill-base.sh's skill_postflight_update) must seed a minimal plan file (even a single all-[COMPLETED]-phase one) or the call fails for a reason unrelated to whatever is actually under test.

To decide whether a failing test suite is caused by your own in-progress edit or by environment/concurrent-sibling drift on a shared source-store tree: temporarily copy the pre-edit file from `git show HEAD:path`, run the suspect suite(s) against it, and compare. Identical failures with the edit entirely absent prove the cause lies elsewhere. Always restore the edited file afterward and diff against a saved copy to confirm byte-for-byte restoration before proceeding.
